security_audit.summary: All 64 static detections are benign documentation examples, placeholders, expected API calls, or attestation terminology. However, the model verification guide omits explicit NRAS JWT signature validation, which can weaken the claimed chain of trust.

remediation.issue: NRAS JWT validation omits explicit cryptographic signature verification.
remediation.suggestion: Require signature verification against trusted NVIDIA keys before reading claims. Then validate issuer, expiration, nonce, overall results, and every per-GPU token.

remediation.issue: Quick-start examples place API key placeholders directly in client constructors.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or a secret manager in every example. State that users must never commit API keys to source control.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete NRAS JWT Authentication Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide tells users to decode NRAS JWTs and inspect claims, but it never explicitly requires cryptographic signature and trusted issuer-key validation. A forged token could satisfy the documented claim checks and undermine attestation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main verification section and final checklist list claim and nonce checks but omit explicit JWT signature verification against a trusted NVIDIA key.

content.user_title: Integrate Verifiable AI with NEAR AI Cloud
content.value_statement: Private AI integrations require careful API and attestation handling. This skill guides OpenAI-compatible requests, TEE verification, and response-signature trust checks.
actual_capabilities: Configures Python and JavaScript OpenAI clients for the NEAR AI Cloud endpoint.
Explains private and anonymised model choices using privacy, context, cost, and capability factors.
Builds model attestation requests with fresh random nonces.
Describes NVIDIA NRAS GPU checks and Intel TDX CPU verification.
Explains how to bind attested signing addresses to chat response signatures.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete executable verifier.
Gateway verification, full chat verification, and encrypted chat are listed as planned.
Model availability, pricing, and endpoint behavior can change after publication.
Usage requires a NEAR AI Cloud account, an API key, and external attestation services.

use_cases.title: Connect an Application
use_cases.description: Configure an existing OpenAI client to send chat requests through NEAR AI Cloud.

use_cases.title: Verify Confidential Inference
use_cases.description: Review nonce, GPU, CPU, and signing-key checks before accepting private inference claims.

use_cases.title: Choose a Privacy Model
use_cases.description: Compare private and anonymised models for sensitive workloads, context needs, and operating cost.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure a Python OpenAI client for NEAR AI Cloud. Use an environment variable for the API key.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the documented private and anonymised models for my workload. Consider privacy, context size, cost, and reasoning needs.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Attestation Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my NEAR AI model attestation flow. Check nonce freshness, NRAS results, TDX verification, signing-address binding, and token expiration.

prompt_templates.title: Design End-to-End Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production verification sequence from attestation request through signed chat response validation. Identify trust anchors, failure states, and stored evidence.

output_examples.input: Configure a secure Python client for a private model.
output: Set the NEAR AI Cloud base URL in the OpenAI client.
Load the API key from an environment variable.
Select a private model and send the chat request.
Generate a fresh nonce and request model attestation.
Validate GPU and CPU evidence before trusting the signing address.
Match the verified signing address to each chat response signature.

output_examples.input: Choose between private and anonymised inference.
output_examples.output: Use private inference for sensitive data requiring TEE isolation. Use anonymised routing when identity separation is sufficient and model choice matters more.

best_practices: Generate a unique 32-byte nonce for every attestation request.
Keep API keys in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Verify GPU, CPU, token freshness, and signing-address binding as one chain.
anti_patterns: Do not trust an attestation only because its overall result is true.
Do not reuse nonces or accept expired attestation tokens.
Do not treat planned gateway or encrypted-chat features as implemented guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill run NEAR AI Cloud requests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration and verification guidance that an agent can apply to your project.

faq.question: Which client libraries can I use?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so Python and JavaScript OpenAI clients are supported examples.

faq.question: What is the difference between private and anonymised models?
faq.answer: Private models run within TEE hardware. Anonymised models remove identifying routing information but do not provide the same isolation claim.

faq.question: Why does model attestation need a nonce?
faq.answer: A fresh nonce binds the evidence to your request and helps prevent replay of stale attestation results.

faq.question: Is NVIDIA GPU attestation enough?
faq.answer: No. The guide also requires Intel TDX verification and binding the attested signing address to the chat signature.

faq.question: Does the skill implement encrypted chat?
faq.answer: No. End-to-end encrypted chat is listed as planned and is not covered by complete implementation instructions.
